open_points.subject: A07 and A13 mapped operation output disclosure
open_points.text: A07 rule 2 says "for an operation node, the class its binding declares for that output" and rule 3 says "A binding output ... takes the class the binding declares ... whatever its inputs' classes"; it then says "A mapped operation over an empty list ... [takes] class by A13 rule 6, not from the binding," while A13 rule 6 assigns "the highest class among the node's inputs."
open_points.question: What class must proof and execution assign to an empty output list from a mapped operation, especially when the binding's declared output class differs from the input classes?
options: Use the binding output's declared class at proof and run time
Use the highest input class at proof and run time
Use the higher of the binding output class and highest input class
open_points.default_guess: Use the higher of the binding output class and highest input class so execution cannot exceed the class proved for downstream delivery.

open_points.subject: A07 failure-detail redaction
open_points.text: A07 rule 5 says a protected `failure_detail` is returned "only as its length and that class."
open_points.question: What does `length` measure: Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, UTF-8 bytes after truncation, or another quantity?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the stored bounded detail
Unicode code points of the stored detail
Original unbounded diagnostic length
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the bounded detail actually stored.

open_points.subject: A07 approval-preview redaction
open_points.text: A07 rule 4 says an agent gets "no built request for a preview any of whose inputs is `personal_data` — only the request's digest."
open_points.question: When any input is personal data, is only the built-request field replaced by its digest while service metadata and individually redacted inputs remain visible, or is the entire preview reduced to the request digest?
options: Redact only the built request
Reduce the entire preview to request digest and class
Keep service metadata but omit all input representations
open_points.default_guess: Redact only the built request, while retaining service metadata and applying normal per-input redaction.

open_points.subject: A07 personal-data file collections
open_points.text: A07 rule 4 says "The same holds for a `personal_data` file: an agent gets its digest and class, and not its size, media type or spool facts," while A13 says a non-empty file list has no aggregate record and consists of element SpooledFiles.
open_points.question: How is a personal-data `many` file reference returned to an agent: one digest for the ordered collection, or an ordered list of per-file digest/class pairs, thereby revealing its cardinality and order?
options: Ordered per-file digest/class pairs
One aggregate digest/class for the collection
Only the class, with neither count nor digests
open_points.default_guess: Return an ordered list of per-file digest/class pairs because no aggregate file-list digest is otherwise defined.

open_points.subject: A17 configuration re-read protection
open_points.text: A17 rule 1 requires the configuration file to be regular, non-symlinked, owner-owned and inaccessible to group or others, but A16 rule 2 says "Exactly four checks apply to a re-read" and lists only parsing and token-list checks; it also says every other start check applies only at restart.
open_points.question: If the configuration file's ownership, permissions, regular-file status or path components change after startup, must a token-list re-read reject it or accept it after only A16's four checks?
options: Repeat all A17 file-security checks on every re-read
Apply only A16's four re-read checks
Stop the kernel when file security changes
open_points.default_guess: Repeat the safe-open and A17 file-security checks on every re-read before accepting the new token list.

open_points.subject: A17 credential header value
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 says the secret file content is "decoded as UTF-8" and "added as that header," but does not define how non-ASCII Unicode is encoded as an HTTP header value.
open_points.question: Are credential values restricted to an ASCII-compatible header-value grammar, encoded as UTF-8 bytes, encoded using an HTTP library's legacy encoding, or refused when non-ASCII?
options: Require printable ASCII
Send UTF-8 bytes
Use the HTTP client's native header encoding
open_points.default_guess: Require printable ASCII excluding controls and leading or trailing whitespace.

open_points.subject: A17 credential control characters
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 refuses a credential that "holds ... a control character."
open_points.question: Which exact characters count as control characters: ASCII C0 and DEL, all Unicode General Category `Cc`, or a broader Unicode control/format set?
options: ASCII C0 plus DEL
All Unicode `Cc` characters
All Unicode control and format characters
open_points.default_guess: Refuse ASCII C0 and DEL, including CR, LF and NUL.

open_points.subject: A17 credential size and newline handling
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 says the file content is decoded as UTF-8 "without one trailing newline" and separately refuses a file "larger than `bounded_text_bytes_max` (A20; read no further)."
open_points.question: Is the credential size ceiling applied to the raw file bytes including the removable trailing newline, or to the credential value after removing that newline?
options: Raw file bytes including the newline
Bytes after removing one trailing LF
Decoded character count after newline removal
open_points.default_guess: Apply the ceiling to raw file bytes before decoding or removing the newline.

open_points.subject: A17 startup header-collision check
open_points.text: A09 rule 1 says an installation whose credential header conflicts with a required or kernel-set header "refuses to start," while A17 does not say what startup does if the selected instance or its manifest record cannot be read well enough to perform that comparison.
open_points.question: Must startup read every selected service's manifest instance to check credential-header collisions, and if so, does a missing or malformed manifest record stop startup or defer the failure to proposal/send time?
options: Read all selected instances and refuse startup on any unreadable record
Check only readable instances and defer other failures
Perform collision checks only when a request is built
open_points.default_guess: Check readable selected instances at startup but defer missing or malformed manifest failures to binding proposal or invocation.

open_points.subject: A17 verbatim credential invariant
open_points.text: A17 states "kernel_writes(verbatim(credential)) INTO {store, record, trace, preview, failure_detail, log, argv, response} -> never," while arbitrary flow inputs, constants, required-header values and service values may independently equal the credential bytes and no rule checks them against credentials.
open_points.question: Is the prohibition based on secret provenance, or must the kernel reject or redact every unrelated value whose bytes happen to equal or contain a credential?
options: Track provenance and prohibit only credential-derived data
Compare all written data against active credential bytes
Limit byte scanning to service response bodies as A09 specifies
open_points.default_guess: Treat the invariant as provenance-based, with explicit byte scanning only for service response bodies.

open_points.subject: Tokens as secrets
open_points.text: State 0 says "service credentials and tokens ... never enter a function, a flow, a trace or an answer"; A16 forbids tokens in responses, while A17's stronger prohibitions on stores, previews, failure details, logs and process arguments are stated only for service credentials.
open_points.question: May owner or agent tokens appear in logs, internal-error diagnostics, stored request data or process arguments, or must they receive the same handling guarantees as service credential values?
options: Apply all A17 non-disclosure guarantees to tokens
Apply only State 0's function/flow/trace/answer prohibition
Rely on the MCP host or proxy to prevent token logging
open_points.default_guess: Apply the same store, trace, diagnostic, log and response prohibitions to tokens as to service credentials.

open_points.subject: Encoded credential returned by a service
open_points.text: State 0 says secrets "never enter ... an answer," but A17 rule 2 says a service response carrying a credential "in another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class," so it may be stored and returned like ordinary output.
open_points.question: Does the State 0 secret guarantee cover transformed or encoded representations of a credential, or only the exact credential bytes the kernel can recognize?
options: Only exact credential bytes are covered
All recognizable encodings must be detected and withheld
Encoded forms may be returned only to the owner regardless of declared class
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the guarantee as covering only exact credential bytes, matching A17's explicit recognition boundary.

open_points.subject: A13 waiting-element executability
open_points.text: A13 rule 2 says an element that waits "does not wait" only for elements run in the pass, while rule 7 says "A waiting element can still execute" even though A13 rule 1 says approval, resolution or resume is required to move a run and A14 says waits do not end themselves.
open_points.question: During ordinary advancement, is a waiting element excluded from readiness until the specific request that clears or retries its wait, or may the scheduler select it again in the same request?
options: Exclude it until an authorized approval, resolution or resume makes it runnable
Allow it to be revisited but prohibit another send
Treat it as ready whenever its input values still exist
open_points.default_guess: Exclude it from readiness until the appropriate request changes or retries its waiting condition.

open_points.subject: A13 propagation versus ready-node scheduling
open_points.text: A13 rule 2 chooses "the ready node with the smallest `node_id`," while rules 4 and 5 cause nodes to conclude without execution when inputs become guarded-off or failed; no rule orders those derived conclusions relative to independently ready executable nodes.
open_points.question: After an execution changes several downstream nodes, must the kernel first exhaust all newly derivable `skipped_by_guard` and `upstream_failed` conclusions, or select the smallest ready executable node first?
options: Exhaust derived conclusions before another execution
Choose globally by node id across executable and derived conclusions
Execute ready nodes first and derive non-executable conclusions only when no node is ready
open_points.default_guess: Process all immediately derivable non-executable conclusions to a fixed point, in the A15 ordering, before selecting the next executable node.

open_points.subject: A13 transitive non-executable waves
open_points.text: A13 rule 4 applies skipping "transitively," and A15 says records of nodes that "become non-executable together" are written in identifier order, but neither defines whether a transitive chain is one group or successive groups.
open_points.question: For a chain of newly skipped or upstream-failed nodes, are all transitively determined records sorted together, or is each propagation wave recorded before deriving the next?
options: Compute the full transitive closure and sort it once
Record breadth-first propagation waves
Record each conclusion immediately, deriving the next afterward
open_points.default_guess: Compute the full currently derivable closure and write its records in (`node_id`, `map_index`) order.

open_points.subject: A13 map element identity
open_points.text: A13 says mapped elements run "in list order" and records use `map_index`, but no rule states the numeric base or exact value assigned to an element's index.
open_points.question: Is `map_index` zero-based, one-based, or another stable representation of list position?
options: Zero-based integer index
One-based integer index
Opaque ordinal generated by the kernel

open_points.subject: A13 multi-output validation
open_points.text: A13 rule 3 says a produced value is validated against its source port and a violation concludes the producing node `contract_violation`, but it gives no order when multiple output ports or multiple elements of a `many` output violate their schemas.
open_points.question: Which failing port or list element determines the recorded failure detail when several produced outputs are invalid?
options: Ports by Unicode name, then list elements by index
Implementation return order
Validate all and record a generic contract violation without identifying one
open_points.default_guess: Use output-port name order and, within a `many` value, the first failing zero-based element.

open_points.subject: A13 derived mapped-list size failure across releases
open_points.text: A13 rule 6 says no record states that a mapped list exceeded `stored_value_bytes_max`; every reader derives the failure from element records and the ceiling. A20 rule 4 allows a new release to change ceilings and says recorded executions are never reinterpreted.
open_points.question: Which ceiling must later readers and startup recovery use when deriving an unrecorded mapped-list failure from an older run?
options: The ceiling of the release that created the run
The current release ceiling
Persist a derived failure or the applicable ceiling with the run
open_points.default_guess: Persist the applicable release ceiling with the run, or record the derived failure, so later releases cannot reinterpret it.
